meta.notes: Seed dataset (v0.1): Australian incidents researched August 2026. Sources include ECAJ 2025 Annual Report, ECAJ Anti-Bullying Rapid Review submission, Menzies Research Centre antisemitism tracker, ABC News, AAP, and specialist outlets. International expansion pending.

incidents.date_note: Incident occurred late Tuesday night (19 August 2026); reported by the Courier Mail on 22 August 2026.
incidents.summary: A McDonald's worker at Cannon Hill, Brisbane yelled "free Palestine" and "free, free Palestine" at two Israeli-Jewish customers and called them "baby killers" after they complained about a missing burger; the worker was stood down pending investigation.
incidents.detail: Late on Tuesday 19 August 2026, Asaf (who asked to have his surname withheld for safety) and his companion Matan visited the McDonald's restaurant in Cannon Hill, Brisbane. After raising with a female staff member that a burger was missing from their order, Asaf said the worker became abusive. She asked where they were from; Asaf said he initially gave a nearby suburb, but when asked again told her he was from Israel, at which point she said "Oh yeah, free Palestine." He began recording as the confrontation escalated. The worker continued yelling "free, free Palestine" and, according to Asaf, called the pair "baby killers" before they were asked to leave. Staff also refused to provide a refund and accused them of lying about the missing items. Asaf said he was left feeling "shaken"; he spoke to police and was directed to the Australian Human Rights Commission. A McDonald's Australia spokesperson confirmed the worker had been stood down pending investigation and issued a sincere apology, citing a zero-tolerance policy for hate and antisemitism. Queensland Jewish Board of Deputies president Jason Steinberg described the company's response as an example of "leadership from the corporate sector" that would help stamp out antisemitism; he stated this was the 100th antisemitic incident reported to the QJBD in 2026.
incidents.slogan_verbatim: Oh yeah, free Palestine; free, free Palestine

sources.name: The Courier Mail (Stella McKenna and Grace Koo)

incidents.caveat: Account based primarily on Asaf's testimony to the Courier Mail. McDonald's confirmed the worker was stood down but did not confirm or deny specific details of the exchange.

incidents.date_note: Described as "last year" in the Courier Mail article published 1 July 2024; precise date not given.
incidents.summary: A classmate held a chair against the throat of a 13-year-old Jewish student and shouted "free Palestine" in his ear; the student was also punched, spat on, given the Nazi salute, and called a "Kike" on an almost daily basis.
incidents.detail: A Queensland Jewish mother, who asked not to be named to protect her children, described sustained antisemitic bullying of her then-13-year-old son at school following the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks. The most serious incident involved a classmate holding a chair against her son's throat and shouting "free Palestine" in his ear. The boy was also punched in the chest, spat at, given the Nazi salute by random students, and called a "Kike". The mother described the abuse as occurring "almost every day." She said it was painful to watch because her son had come to accept the bullying as normal: "The sad thing about it for me is he just accepts that it's okay, he thinks it's normal to be bullied because you're Jewish." Queensland Jewish Board of Deputies president Jason Steinberg noted that teachers expressing antisemitic political views had become a new and disturbing phenomenon, with some using "factually incorrect information" about Israel in front of students.
incidents.caveat: Identity of school not disclosed. Mother asked not to be named. Incident described retrospectively in a July 2024 article; precise date within 2023 not given.

incidents.summary: Joel, a Jewish man on holiday from Victoria, was spat on after replying "free the hostages" to the chants of a pro-Palestinian rally in Surfers Paradise; a 54-year-old man was charged with common assault.
incidents.detail: On 11 May 2024, Joel, a Jewish man visiting Queensland from Victoria, encountered a pro-Palestinian rally in Surfers Paradise which he described as "vile and anti-Semitic." After hearing the crowd's chants he called out "free the hostages," following which two men followed him. The incident was captured on video; two men were seen approaching Joel before a spitting sound could be heard. Joel said the perpetrator "spat in my mouth" and that he subsequently required genetic and disease testing. He told the Courier Mail he had since begun hiding signs of being Jewish and did not want to return to the Gold Coast, where he owns a unit. A 54-year-old man was charged with common assault and listed to appear at Southport Magistrates Court on 11 July 2024.
incidents.legal_outcome: A 54-year-old man charged with common assault; listed to appear at Southport Magistrates Court on 11 July 2024.
incidents.caveat: The specific words of the rally chants directed at Joel are not quoted verbatim in the source. The protest context was pro-Palestinian; slogan_verbatim is set to null accordingly.

incidents.summary: Zayne McMillan posed as if firing a weapon on the Bondi footbridge, yelled "Free Palestine" then "F*** the Jews" and threatened a Jewish man and his family; he was jailed for 12 months.
incidents.detail: On 31 January 2026, Zayne Jason William McMillan, 23, a First Nations bricklayer, posed as if holding a firearm on the Bondi Beach footbridge — the site used in the IS-inspired December 2025 Hanukkah massacre — while a friend photographed him. He then yelled "Free Palestine" and, after being challenged, "F*** the Jews", and threatened a 47-year-old Jewish man walking with his family. He also intimidated a second visibly Jewish man walking with his son to a synagogue. McMillan pleaded guilty to three counts of offensive behaviour and two counts of intimidation. On 21 April 2026, Judge Michael Barko sentenced him to 12 months' jail with a nine-month non-parole period. The judge rejected the "not an antisemite" defence, noting that during roughly 35 minutes of conduct, "not one other faith, belief or culture was referred to."
incidents.legal_outcome: Zayne Jason William McMillan, 23, pleaded guilty to three counts of offensive behaviour and two counts of intimidation. Sentenced 21 April 2026 by Judge Michael Barko to 12 months' jail with a nine-month non-parole period.

incidents.date_note: Occurred in the early hours of 29 November 2025 (approximately two weeks before the Bondi Hanukkah attack of 14 December 2025).
incidents.location: North Bondi, Sydney, New South Wales
incidents.summary: Buildings and bollards at North Bondi Beach were scrawled with "Free Palestine, F*** Israel" and similar messages approximately two weeks before the 14 December 2025 IS-inspired Hanukkah massacre at the same location.
incidents.detail: In the early hours of 29 November 2025, buildings and bollards in North Bondi were scrawled with "Free Palestine, F*** Israel", "Israel commits genocide", "F*** the IDF", and "Israel has blood on their hands." The "Head On" photo exhibition, lifeguard towers, barriers, and other beachfront infrastructure were also targeted. Police released CCTV images of two slim-built men aged around 20 last seen on Campbell Parade. Further graffiti was found on Ramsgate Avenue around 4 am. Bondi Beach is a historically significant location for Sydney's Jewish community. Whether the graffiti was connected to the subsequent attack was not established by police.
incidents.caveat: No link established by police between this graffiti and the December 2025 terror attack.

incidents.summary: On the second anniversary of the 7 October Hamas attacks, "Glory to Hamas" was painted on a Fitzroy billboard and "Free Palestine" and "Oct 7, do it again" appeared on a nearby building; Victoria Police and the AFP investigated whether the graffiti constituted a terrorism offence.
incidents.detail: On the second anniversary of the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023, "Glory to Hamas" was painted on a billboard at Alexandra Parade and Brunswick Street, Fitzroy. "Free Palestine" and "Oct 7, do it again" appeared on a building further along Alexandra Parade near Smith Street. Similar "do it again" graffiti appeared in Westgarth. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called the graffiti "abhorrent"; Premier Jacinta Allan and Opposition Leader Sussan Ley condemned it. ECAJ co-CEO Alex Ryvchin called it despicable. Victoria Police and the Australian Federal Police jointly investigated whether the graffiti constituted a terrorism offence.
incidents.slogan_verbatim: Free Palestine; Oct 7, do it again; Glory to Hamas

incidents.summary: Gladstone Park Secondary College students chanted "free, free Palestine" at Grade 5 Mount Scopus Memorial College students on excursion at the Melbourne Museum, then called them "dirty Jews" and "baby killers."
incidents.detail: During a shared visit to the Melbourne Museum on 24 July 2025, students from Gladstone Park Secondary College (aged approximately 16–17) chanted "free, free Palestine" at Grade 5 students (aged 10–11) from Mount Scopus Memorial College, a Jewish school. The older students then called the younger children "dirty Jews" and "baby killers." Mount Scopus principal Dan Sztrajt said a student "got a tap on the shoulder, turned around and the vitriol started." One parent reported his 10-year-old son was "terrified"; another's grandfather said his granddaughter was "totally traumatised" and had no understanding of why she was being called a "baby killer" and a "dirty Jew." Gladstone Park principal Veronica Hoy issued an apology, calling the conduct "completely deplorable."

incidents.date_note: The synagogue was graffitied twice on 22 June 2025 (Sunday afternoon and again Sunday evening). It was one of six attacks on the premises between March and August 2025.
incidents.summary: The heritage-listed Melbourne Hebrew Congregation was graffitied twice in one day with "Free Palestine" and "Iran is da bomb" inside a mushroom cloud; a 37-year-old man was later charged over six attacks on the synagogue.
incidents.detail: The Melbourne Hebrew Congregation synagogue on Toorak Road, South Yarra, a heritage-listed building, was graffitied twice on 22 June 2025 — once in the afternoon and again in the evening after the earlier markings were removed — with "Free Palestine" and "Iran is da bomb" (written inside a mushroom cloud). The vandalism occurred less than 12 hours after the United States joined Israel in coordinated airstrikes on Iran's nuclear facilities. Victoria Police subsequently arrested a 37-year-old man over six attacks on the synagogue (on 11 March, 21 June, 22 June, 22 July, 30 July, and 19 August 2025), some of which were carried out while wearing a "Ghostface" mask.
incidents.slogan_verbatim: Free Palestine; Iran is da bomb
incidents.legal_outcome: A 37-year-old man was charged over six attacks on the synagogue between March and August 2025, some carried out wearing a "Ghostface" mask.

incidents.summary: An elderly disabled Jewish woman reported that a Vodafone store employee in Elsternwick repeatedly shouted "Free Palestine" at her, called her a "dirty Zionist", said "Jews are disgusting", and filmed her without consent; she told the Anti-Defamation Commission the slogan "felt like a call for my murder."
incidents.detail: An elderly disabled Jewish woman reported that a Vodafone store employee in Elsternwick, Melbourne, repeatedly shouted "Free Palestine" at her, called her a "dirty Zionist", said "Jews are disgusting", and demanded her phone and filmed her without consent. She told Anti-Defamation Commission director Dr Dvir Abramovich: "Him saying Free Palestine to me basically felt like a call for my murder." The employee was stood down and later left the company. Vodafone's internal review disputed aspects of the account, stating that key claims were not supported by their information including the nature and tone of the interaction or the customer being prevented from leaving. No criminal charge was reported.

incidents.detail: Logged in the ECAJ 2025 Annual Report and reproduced in the Menzies Research Centre antisemitism tracker. A man pushed a Jewish male off his bike by shoving his shoulder near a Melbourne synagogue, while yelling "f****** Jews", "Free Palestine", and "You kikes" at the group of Jewish people present.

incidents.summary: The Southern Sydney Synagogue in Allawah was daubed with "Free Palestine", "Hitler on top", "F*** Israel Jew dogs", and approximately a dozen red and black Nazi swastikas.
incidents.detail: The Southern Sydney Synagogue (Allawah) was vandalised with "Free Palestine", "Hitler on top", "F*** Israel Jew dogs", "Jew Dogs", a reference to "Allah", and about a dozen red and black Nazi swastikas. Two men were subsequently charged: Kye Pickering (26) on 26 June 2025 with property damage, displaying a Nazi symbol, and participating in a criminal group; and Tarek Zahabe (27) on 17 July 2025 with directing and participating in a criminal group.
incidents.legal_outcome: Kye Pickering, 26, charged 26 June 2025 with property damage over $2,000 in company, public display of a Nazi symbol, and participating in a criminal group. Tarek Zahabe, 27, charged 17 July 2025 with directing/participating in a criminal group. Both listed to appear at Downing Centre Local Court, October 2025.
incidents.caveat: NSW Police later alleged some early-2025 Sydney antisemitic attacks were staged by an organised-crime network; this case is part of that cluster, complicating grassroots motive attribution. The criminal charges were confirmed regardless of motive.

incidents.date_note: Reported during 2025; however, an Israellycool article dated 5 September 2024 covers an apparently identical incident targeting the same school, suggesting this may have occurred in 2024. Precise date not confirmed.
incidents.summary: An Instagram group operating under the name "Free Palestine Printing" published the faces of a Melbourne rabbi and pupils at a Jewish school; ECAJ co-CEO Alex Ryvchin described the group as "the Der Sturmer arm of the anti-Israel movement."
incidents.detail: An Instagram account operating under the name "Free Palestine Printing" posted the faces of a Melbourne rabbi and students at a Jewish school, constituting targeted online exposure of Jewish individuals including minors. Antisemitism envoy Jillian Segal and ECAJ co-CEO Alex Ryvchin condemned the posts. Ryvchin described the group as "the Der Sturmer arm of the anti-Israel movement."
incidents.caveat: The "Free Palestine" slogan appears in the group's name and declared purpose rather than as a chant in the moment of harm. This incident is included on the basis that the harmful act — doxxing Jewish children — was carried out explicitly in the name and advancement of the slogan, making the nexus organisational rather than verbal. The year is listed as 2025 but an Israellycool article dated 5 September 2024 covers an apparently identical incident; the true date should be verified.

incidents.summary: An occupant of a vehicle yelled "F*** Jews" and "Free Palestine" at people outside a Melbourne synagogue.
incidents.detail: Logged in the ECAJ 2025 Annual Report and reproduced in the Menzies Research Centre antisemitism tracker. An occupant of a passing vehicle yelled "F*** Jews" and "Free Palestine" at people gathered outside a synagogue in Melbourne.

incidents.summary: Around 200 "Free Palestine Melbourne" protesters gathered at Princes Park adjacent to the Central Shule Chabad synagogue during Shabbat, forcing evacuation of the service; bottles and racial slurs were thrown, and cars with Palestinian flags drove through Caulfield harassing and spitting at Jewish passers-by.
incidents.detail: Following a suspicious fire at a Palestinian-owned burger shop in Caulfield (later found unrelated to the Jewish community), about 200 protesters operating under the banner of "Free Palestine Melbourne" gathered at Princes Park directly opposite the Central Shule Chabad synagogue during Friday Shabbat services. The synagogue was evacuated for the safety of congregants. Bottles and other projectiles were thrown towards Jews outside the synagogue; racial slurs were directed at Jewish people. Cars bearing Palestinian flags drove through Caulfield with occupants verbally harassing and spitting at visibly Jewish passers-by. One man was arrested.
incidents.legal_outcome: One man arrested at the scene.
incidents.caveat: This is a protest-context incident. The "Free Palestine" slogan was the declared banner of the group that targeted the synagogue and its attendees; it was not a passing individual using the slogan as a weapon. Whether the slogan was chanted in the same moment as specific slurs is not separately documented; the nexus is via the group's identity and deliberate targeting of a Jewish institution.

incidents.summary: A 44-year-old Jewish man was surrounded and beaten by a pro-Palestinian crowd chanting "Free Palestine" at a children's playground in south Sydney; he suffered spinal fractures and a concussion and said he was "very lucky" to be alive.
incidents.detail: A 44-year-old Jewish man was at a children's playground in south Sydney when he tore down a half-removed poster for a pro-Palestinian rally. Another man in the playground approached him, asked if he supported Israel, and then threatened "I will murder you." The Jewish man called the police but was surrounded by a crowd of men and women yelling slurs. He was hit in the head, fell, and was beaten by multiple assailants who punched and kicked him while calling him "pro-Jew dog" and other slurs. He was hospitalised for four days with spinal fractures, facial injuries, and a concussion. He told Sky News Australia he was "very lucky" to be alive. Police were investigating.
incidents.caveat: Specific suburb within south Sydney not identified in available reporting.
